expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: "If the migration lands before the last old pod drains, every request hitting those three paths errors until rollout finishes."

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: "PR A (today, safe): code stops reading legacy_email... PR B (Tuesday): the DROP, after PR A has baked long enough."

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: "Nothing restores it. Not git revert, not a redeploy. The only path back is a point-in-time restore of the whole database."

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: "Rolling back PR A is two minutes and any one person can do it. Recovering from a bad DROP is a multi-hour lossy restore needing someone with prod credentials."

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: "Recovering from a bad DROP is... on a Friday evening."

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: "a CI check that fails when a migration containing DROP or a destructive ALTER lands in the same diff as application code."

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: "Short answer: merge the code change, hold the DROP."

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: "The code change (stop reading the column) is fully reversible... The DROP is... belongs in its own deploy."
